title: Random forests on routine blood and urine tests separate epilepsy from nonepileptic events
summary: Random forest models were built on routine body fluid test data from West China Hospital (2009-2019) and validated on data collected prospectively in 2020-2022 from 388 patients in total (218 epilepsy, 170 PNEE). Validation AUROCs were 80.0% for electrolyte and 79.0% for urine models. Selected characteristics were then put into logistic regression nomograms with C statistics of 0.79 and 0.85.
ai_technology: Random forest models on routine electrolyte, blood cell, metabolism and urine tests
organization: Sichuan University; West China Hospital of Sichuan University

evidence.tested: Training on 2009-2019 register data and prospective validation on 2020-2022 patients.
evidence.unknown: Single center; modest AUROC; nomograms rest on logistic regression; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests ranked body fluid characteristics and predicted epilepsy versus psychogenic nonepileptic events.
